unit: Rufus Vane operated a small sawmill up river and resided in a desolate clearing surrounded by stumps. He married Lorna Ainslie after coercing her into the union by threatening to foreclose on her widowed mother's farm mortgage. During their marriage, his household took in the orphan Nell Harcourt for over two years to help care for their eight young children, including three sets of twins. After Rufus passed away, his household was dissolved and his children were distributed among family members, leading Nell to be sent to the Marden asylum. It was later revealed that Rufus had sailed to Cuba on the Four Sisters, contracted yellow fever, and died there thirteen years prior to the events at Seven Gulls; the man who had returned to Seven Gulls in his place and lived under his name as an invalid for eleven years was actually his cousin, Laurence Vane.

label: History
value: At Wexcombe, Hugh earns High Honors in Classics.
unit: Hugh grows up in Brierley, having spent three childhood years in Alberta with his father. Upon returning from a summer in New Brunswick, he re-enters Brierley school, where he becomes a fierce academic rival to Nell Harcourt after pulling her braid and getting her slate broken over his head. Though he apologizes, Nell holds a grudge against him, even when he defends her to the teacher or tries to offer gifts. Hugh attends Regent's Academy alongside Nell, entering the advanced classes and competing closely with her for top honors. He later serves as the president of the Brierley Village Improvement Society, advocating for local beautification projects. To pay for his medical degree at Wexcombe College, he works as a schoolteacher at Pale Sands. At Wexcombe, he excels academically, becomes Captain of the Freshman football team, wins the Cooper Prize, and earns High Honors in Classics.
